topic.label: Art History
topic.desc: Art History: the study of visual art and architecture across periods and cultures through formal, contextual and theoretical analysis.

concepts: Description and analysis of composition, line, colour, space and medium in a work of art.
Identification of subjects, symbols and attributes and interpretation of their cultural meaning.
Major Western art periods from antiquity through the Renaissance, Baroque and modernism.
Buildings, urban spaces and architectural theory from ancient temples to modern design.
Art of Asia, Africa, the Americas, Oceania and the Islamic world studied in its own terms and contexts.
Collecting, provenance research, display and theoretical approaches such as feminism, social history and postcolonialism.
skills: Writes a formal description of an artwork and checks every visual claim against the image.
Compares two works side by side for form and technique and checks the comparison against catalog data.
Identifies medium and technique from visual and technical evidence and checks it against conservation reports.
Identifies subjects, saints, deities and attributes in an image and checks them against iconographic dictionaries.
Interprets an artwork's cultural meaning in Panofsky's sense and checks the reading against period texts.
Analyses allegorical and mythological programs and checks sources against classical and religious texts.
Attributes an unknown work to a period, school or artist by style and checks it against dated comparanda.
Builds a timeline of artists and movements and checks dates against reference sources.
Analyses patronage and commission context for a work and checks facts against archival documents.
Analyses a building's plan, elevation and structure and checks measurements against survey drawings.
Identifies architectural styles such as Gothic or modernist and checks diagnostic features against reference works.
Traces the history of an urban space and checks phases against maps and building records.
Interprets a non-Western work within its own cultural categories and checks the account against specialist scholarship.
Analyses artistic exchange along trade and colonial routes and checks the claims against dated objects.
Analyses geometric ornament and calligraphy and checks inscriptions and patterns against published readings.
Reconstructs an object's ownership history and checks every link against sale catalogs and archives, flagging gaps.
Critiques an exhibition's display and narrative and checks claims against the catalog and labels.
Applies feminist, social history or postcolonial theory to a work and checks the argument for evidence.
mcp: Enhance responses with scholarly research and citations
